title: ECG Lead Placement & Paper
body:
## Limb leads and colors

| Electrode | Position | AHA color | IEC color |
|---|---|---|---|
| RA | Right arm / right shoulder or forearm | White | Red |
| LA | Left arm / left shoulder or forearm | Black | Yellow |
| RL | Right leg / right lower abdomen or thigh (ground) | Green | Black |
| LL | Left leg / left lower abdomen or thigh | Red | Green |

AHA mnemonics: *white on right*, *smoke over fire* (black above red on the left), *clouds over grass* (white above green on the right).

- **3-lead**: RA, LA, LL only — Einthoven's triangle. Monitors leads I, II and III. Lead `II` shows P waves best.
- **5-lead**: the four limb electrodes plus one brown chest electrode, usually at `V1`. Gives all six limb leads plus one precordial.
- **12-lead**: four limb plus six precordial. Twelve views, ten electrodes.

## Precordial (chest) leads

| Lead | Landmark | AHA color |
|---|---|---|
| `V1` | 4th intercostal space, **right** sternal border | Red |
| `V2` | 4th intercostal space, **left** sternal border | Yellow |
| `V3` | Midway between `V2` and `V4` — place it last of the first four | Green |
| `V4` | 5th intercostal space, midclavicular line | Blue |
| `V5` | Anterior axillary line, horizontal with `V4` | Orange |
| `V6` | Midaxillary line, horizontal with `V4` | Purple |

**Counting method:** find the sternal notch, slide down to the bony ridge (sternal angle / angle of Louis) — the 2nd rib attaches there. The space just below it is the 2nd intercostal space. Count down: 3rd, 4th. Place `V1` and `V2` there, then find the 5th space for `V4`, then fill in `V3`, then `V5` and `V6` level with `V4` — not along the rib.

> **Trap:** `V1` and `V2` placed one or two spaces too high is the single most common 12-lead error. It fakes an anteroseptal infarct pattern, inverts P waves in `V1`–`V2`, and can create a false Brugada look.

## Extra views

| Set | Placement | Use |
|---|---|---|
| Right-sided (`V1R`–`V6R`) | Mirror image on the right chest; `V4R` (5th space, right midclavicular line) is the one that matters | Inferior STEMI — look for right ventricular infarct. `0.5 mm` of ST elevation in `V4R` is positive. Changes management: those patients are preload-dependent, so **no nitroglycerin** |
| Posterior (`V7`–`V9`) | Same horizontal level as `V6`: `V7` posterior axillary line, `V8` mid-scapular line, `V9` left paraspinal border | Posterior MI, especially with tall R waves and ST depression in `V1`–`V3`. `0.5 mm` of elevation is diagnostic |

## Skin prep

1. Position supine or semi-Fowler's, arms relaxed and supported, legs uncrossed. Expose and drape.
2. Pick flat, fleshy skin — avoid bone, breast tissue and large muscle bellies.
3. Clip excess hair; do not shave.
4. Clean with alcohol or soap and water and let it dry completely.
5. Lightly abrade with a dry gauze or the prep patch on the electrode.
6. Check the gel is moist and the electrodes are in date.
7. Press firmly, leave a stress loop in the cable so nothing pulls.

## Artifact troubleshooting

| Artifact | Looks like | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Wandering baseline | Slow rolling drift | Re-prep skin, secure loose electrodes, ask the patient to breathe normally, remove lotion |
| Somatic / muscle tremor | Fuzzy irregular fine noise | Warm the patient, support the arms, calm tremor; consider Mason-Likar torso placement for monitoring only |
| `60 Hz` AC interference | Uniform thick fuzzy band, perfectly regular | Unplug nearby equipment, untangle and uncross cables, check the ground electrode and outlet |
| One flat lead | Single straight line | That electrode or wire is disconnected or dried out |
| All leads flat | Nothing anywhere | Cable unplugged from the machine, or the patient is in asystole — check the patient first |

## Paper and boxes

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Standard speed | `25 mm/s` (`50 mm/s` doubles horizontal spread) |
| Standard gain | `10 mm/mV` — the calibration box should be `10 mm` tall |
| Small box | `1 mm` = `0.04 s` across, `0.1 mV` up |
| Large box | `5 mm` = `0.20 s` across, `0.5 mV` up |
| 5 large boxes | `1 second` |
| 30 large boxes | `6 seconds` — the rhythm strip |

## Three ways to get the rate

1. **300 method** (regular): `300 / large boxes between R waves`. Memorize the sequence `300, 150, 100, 75, 60, 50, 43`.
2. **1500 method** (regular, precise): `1500 / small boxes between R waves`.
3. **6-second method** (irregular — the only honest one for atrial fibrillation): count QRS complexes in a `6 s` strip and multiply by `10`.

## Normal intervals

| Interval | Normal | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| P wave | under `0.12 s`, under `2.5 mm` tall | Atrial depolarization |
| PR | `0.12–0.20 s` (`3–5` small boxes) | Longer = AV block; shorter with a delta wave = pre-excitation |
| QRS | `0.06–0.10 s`; `0.12 s` or more is wide | Wide means the beat did not use the normal conduction system |
| QT | varies with rate; roughly less than half the R-R at normal rates | Ventricular depolarization plus repolarization |
| QTc (Bazett: `QT / square root of RR in seconds`) | up to `0.44 s` men, `0.46 s` women | `0.47/0.48 s` prolonged; `0.50 s` or more is torsades risk |

## Lead groups: what wall, what artery

| Leads | Wall | Usual artery |
|---|---|---|
| `II`, `III`, `aVF` | Inferior | Right coronary artery (about `80%`), sometimes left circumflex |
| `V1`, `V2` | Septal | LAD, septal branches |
| `V3`, `V4` | Anterior | LAD |
| `V5`, `V6` | Low lateral / apical | LAD or left circumflex |
| `I`, `aVL` | High lateral | Left circumflex or first diagonal |
| `V7`–`V9` (or tall R + ST depression in `V1`–`V3`) | Posterior | Left circumflex or RCA |
| `V4R` | Right ventricle | Proximal RCA |
| `aVR` elevated with widespread ST depression | Global ischemia | Left main or three-vessel disease |

> **Key:** ST elevation in `II`, `III`, `aVF` always earns a right-sided `V4R` before anyone reaches for nitroglycerin.
